name: Process Stripe refunds with Allowly approval and reviewer checks

parameters.errorMessage: Refund stopped. Inspect the decision or review result; do not bypass the checks.

parameters.escalationNote: Customer-reported outcome from the authenticated demo review endpoint.

parameters.content:
## Process Stripe refunds with Allowly approval and reviewer checks

### How it works
Run one USD test refund per execution. The workflow checks a stored Allowly authorization before calling Stripe. An allowed request proceeds; a denied request stops. Confirmation or escalation pauses for an authenticated reviewer, then requires a fresh allow decision for the same refund details.

The output keeps the Stripe refund ID and status alongside the Allowly decision receipt. Receipt signing may be pending; this workflow does not verify signatures. A decision receipt does not prove that a refund completed.

### Setup
1. On self-hosted n8n, install **n8n-nodes-allowly 0.2.1** and allow Code nodes.
2. Follow the [full setup guide](https://github.com/Allowly-AI/n8n-nodes-allowly/blob/main/examples/stripe-refund-with-approval.md) to create the refund policy and store one authorization.
3. Create a succeeded USD Stripe test payment. Select the **same Stripe test credential** on both Stripe HTTP nodes.
4. Select the **same Allowly API credential** on all Allowly nodes and **Fetch decision receipt**.
5. Set a dedicated **Header Auth** credential on **Wait for reviewer**. Keep the review secret separate from API keys.
6. Fill **Refund request** with the stored authorization, payment ID, stable request ID, and amount in cents. Run the full workflow from **Run test refund**, with no pinned data.

**Test mode only.** Do not run the refund node alone. Keep the request ID and fields unchanged on retries; reconcile uncertain refunds in Stripe first. Production use needs durable refund tracking and reconciliation.

## 1. Prepare one refund request
Edit **Refund request** before running. Use integer cents, USD, and a stable request ID. Validation freezes the details used by the policy check, reviewer, and Stripe. Run one request per full execution.

## 2. Check the payment and policy
Only a matching, succeeded Stripe test payment continues. Allowly checks the stored authorization: allow proceeds, confirm or escalate requires review, and deny stops. Invalid responses and errors stop the workflow.

## 3. Review the frozen request
Within four minutes, POST to the execution's resume URL using Header Auth. Send only boolean `approved` and the exact `resource` from **Validate request**. Validation binds the response to this refund before resolving the Allowly review.

## 4. Require a fresh allow
After approval, recheck the original authorization and unchanged refund details. Only a fresh allow reaches Stripe. Rejection, timeout, or any other decision stops; approval alone cannot create the refund.

## 5. Create the Stripe test refund
Use the same Stripe test credential as **Read Stripe payment**. Unchanged retries reuse the request ID and fields; Stripe's duplicate protection is time-limited. Save **Refund result**, including its refund ID and status.

## 6. Retain decision evidence
Save the refund result with its decision receipt. Signing may be pending; signatures are not verified here. If receipt retrieval fails, recover it separately using **Refund result**. Do not create another refund to recover evidence.
